lesson.subtitle: Lesson 25 -- Review & Simulation: Full Deal Discussion
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Eduarda | Lesson 25 -- Review & Simulation: Full Deal Discussion

listenings.text: Hi Eduarda, it's James. Tomorrow is the big one: the meeting with NorthPack. A few reminders. Mark Holloway will put ninety million on the table, and he will ask for exclusivity. Don't agree to exclusivity until the price is closer to a hundred. Remember, the family's deal-breaker is the team. Three years of job protection is non-negotiable. If Mark raises a red flag, don't panic and don't argue. Thank him and say we will come back with the data. And keep the momentum. A deal that stops for a month often dies. Call me after the meeting.

In a full deal discussion, you rarely use one skill at a time. You open with small talk and a smooth transition. You make proposals with conditionals: if you did this, we would do that. You soften difficult points with hedging, so that the other side doesn't feel attacked. And you use rhetorical questions to keep both sides focused on the shared goal. The best negotiators also prepare before the meeting starts. They separate what is negotiable from what is not. And they never end a meeting without a clear next step, even a small one.

extra_audio.text: Eduarda met Mark Holloway, the CEO of NorthPack. After a little small talk, she got down to business. Mark put ninety million on the table and asked for exclusivity. Eduarda said the price might be slightly low. She explained that job losses were a deal-breaker for the family. In the end, they agreed on the main principles and kept the momentum.
